title: UniCon: Unified Framework for Efficient Contrastive Alignment via Kernels
claim: Paired inputs are encoded and compared into one similarity weight matrix, from which linear and nonlinear cases both yield efficient closed-form solutions.
layout: Single wide panel, left-to-right flow: paired inputs, encoders, similarity matrix, weight matrix, with orange and blue feedback loops arching over and under the top and bottom
description: A wide single-panel diagram reading left to right. At far left, a stack of text captions (x) and a stack of photos of a green tractor (y) feed into two trapezoid encoders, f_theta2 (cream) and f_theta1 (yellow), inside a dashed blue box labeled with F^T F. Encoder outputs become row and column feature cells, f_theta1(x_i) down the left and f_theta2(y_j) across the top. These form a green n-by-n grid of similarities s_ij with an orange diagonal for positive pairs. An arrow leads to a matrix S(gamma) of gamma_ij entries, with an orange diagonal and purple shades of varying intensity. Two long return arrows run back to the encoders: an orange one labeled 'Linear (with SVD)' and a blue one labeled 'Nonlinear (with kernels)'. Orange 'Hyper-spherical Similarity' text sits beneath the grid. The eye goes first to the colored grids.
caption: Unified Framework for Efficient Contrastive Alignment via Kernels (UniCon). Starting from paired inputs, UniCon builds a contrastive similarity weight matrix $S(\gamma)$ using hyper-spherical similarities, then computes either (i) a closed-form spectral update in the linear case (orange) or (ii) a kernelized solution in the nonlinear case (blue).
abstract: Contrastive objectives power state-of-the-art multimodal models, but their training remains slow, relying on long stochastic optimization. We propose a Unified Framework for Efficient Contrastive Alignment via Kernels (UniCon), which spans linear and nonlinear encoders as well as one-to-one and many-to-many alignments. At its core, UniCon introduces the contrastive similarity weight matrix $S(Î³)$, which enables closed-form global solutions that provably replace minibatch back-propagation with exact updates. Through the lens of reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces (RKHS), UniCon provides a kernelized perspective that unifies contrastive alignment and reveals its connection to spectral methods. To validate the theory, we conduct experiments on synthetic, unimodal, multimodal, and zero-shot tasks, demonstrating that UniCon achieves substantial efficiency gains while preserving generality and strong empirical performance.
